notices.title: Valkyries victory parade on the Embarcadero today, Wednesday, Nov 4, noon to 2 pm
notices.detail: The parade runs along the Embarcadero from the Ferry Building near Mission Street to Second and King streets; fans can gather from 9 am. The Embarcadero, King Street and nearby blocks (including Market between Drumm and Steuart, and Mission, Howard, Folsom, Harrison and Bryant between Main and the Embarcadero) close in stages from 12:01 am or 8 am until 4 pm. Muni's F and N lines along the Embarcadero are suspended about 9:30 am to 3 pm, with a bus replacing them. BART and Bay Ferry are adding service. The City recommends transit.
notices.stripLine: Embarcadero closed; F and N suspended

notices.title: Election results: updated preliminary counts about 4 pm daily, Nov 4 to 13 (not Nov 11)
notices.detail: The Department of Elections posts a daily estimate of ballots left to count starting Nov 4 and updated preliminary results at about 4 pm each day from Nov 4 through Nov 13, except Veterans Day, then more updates as counting continues. Mail ballots postmarked by Election Day count if they arrive within seven days. The earliest certification date is Wednesday, Nov 25; final results must be certified by Dec 3.
notices.oneLiner: Election results update about 4 pm daily through Nov 13; certification due by Dec 3

notices.title: Southbound US-101 fully closed from the 9th Street/Civic Center exit to Cesar Chavez, Friday 11 pm to Monday 6 am (Nov 6 to 9)
notices.detail: Caltrans paving work at the Hospital Curve. Detours use southbound I-280 via 6th Street and southbound Potrero; SFMTA parking control officers will help at key detour points. The same weekend, northbound I-280 near the Farallones Street overcrossing has overnight lane closures (at least one lane open).
notices.stripLine: Southbound 101 shut Fri night to Mon

notices.title: Veterans Day, Wednesday, Nov 11: meters enforced, libraries closed, trash pickup as normal
notices.detail: SFMTA enforces parking meters, nightly street sweeping (midnight to 6 am), white zones and safety rules. Not enforced: residential permit time limits, general time limits, weekday daytime street sweeping and unmetered yellow and green zones. Recology collects as normal. All San Francisco Public Library locations are closed. The Board of Supervisors meets as scheduled on Tuesday, Nov 10.

notices.title: Northbound US-101 connector to the Central Freeway fully closed, Friday 11 pm to Monday 6 am (Nov 13 to 16)
notices.detail: Caltrans work on the Central Viaduct and I-80 Bayshore Viaduct. Detours will be signed; SFMTA says details will follow.
notices.stripLine: 101 to Central Freeway shut Fri to Mon

posts.gist: Election Day: 501 polling places and the City Hall Voting Center open 7 am to 8 pm; four preliminary results reports after polls close.
Mayor signs legislation strengthening San Francisco's wholesale produce market.
Mayor announces the Nov 4 victory parade for the WNBA champion Golden State Valkyries along the Embarcadero.
Mayor signs legislation expanding the landmark at the site of the Compton's Cafeteria riot.
Mayor signs legislation on renter protections against unwarranted evictions and hidden rental fees.
Mayor signs legislation streamlining the process to build housing.
Mayor declares a local emergency to prepare for El Niño.
Mayor introduces legislation for Freedom West 2.0 in the Western Addition, which could bring nearly 2,400 homes, more than 17% expected to be affordable.
Mayor marks upgrades to three public basketball courts with the Valkyries and Warriors.
Mayor reports an 84% drop in speeding where automated speed cameras operate.

benchmarks.note: FBI figures for 2024, the latest year with matching city, state and national numbers. Rates are offenses reported to police per 100,000 residents (FBI population for San Francisco: 802,856). San Francisco's rates fell from 2023 (violent 710.2, property 5,712.5). The many people who work in or visit San Francisco aren't counted as residents, which pushes per-resident rates up. The FBI advises against ranking places on these numbers alone.

source.label: DataSF, Police Department Incident Reports: 2018 to Present

charts.note: Everything SFPD writes a report on, from theft to warrants and lost property. Reports appear once a supervisor approves them, so October 2026 can still rise. Per the City's notes, some reports are removed under court orders or during active investigations.

charts.title: Property and violent crime reports per month
charts.sub: Distinct incidents, by the date they happened

source.label: DataSF, Police Department Incident Reports: 2018 to Present

charts.note: Property: the larceny theft, burglary, motor vehicle theft and arson categories. Violent: the assault, robbery, rape and homicide categories. These are SFPD report categories, not the FBI's: assault here includes simple assault, which the FBI's violent crime rate leaves out. Reports appear once a supervisor approves them, so October 2026 can still rise.

charts.note: Calls to the 911 call center that sent an officer out, plus incidents officers saw and logged in the field. Only closed calls are counted, so the latest days can be incomplete.
